The Senior Cloud Engineer will be accountable for driving the configuration and operation of University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) cloud infrastructure services.
The Senior Cloud Engineer will coordinate the partnership with a broad range of developers, engineers, business partners, and key University stakeholders to provide best-in-class cloud services.
This role configures and facilitates workloads in the cloud, automates cloud infrastructure maintenance, and builds new operational monitoring capabilities.
The Senior Cloud Engineer will positively impact UCSF's operations and culture by ensuring UCSF's Information Technology (IT) infrastructure is operable, secure, efficient, and effective in service of the University's mission.
The Senior Cloud Engineer will advance the University's mission by delivering exceptional information technology services comprehensively and consistently across customers and stakeholders.

Department Overview
University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) is distinguished as a leading academic healthcare organization, home to groundbreaking discoveries, world-class education, and exceptional healthcare services.
Infrastructure Services (IS) is the backbone of the technological infrastructure, assuring the technical services that enable the academic, medical, and research missions of the organization.
Beyond a focus on maintaining systems and resolving issues, we are committed to nurturing the potential of our team members and empowering them to excel.
UCSF Infrastructure Services provides 24x7 support to the University community, always upholding the highest level of responsiveness and reliability for our customers.

The team oversees the management and maintenance of various technology platforms, including system and cloud services, to guarantee they are secure, readily available, and performing optimally.
Platform Services handles the management of critical software, such as Epic, ensuring it supports the highest level of medical service delivery by operating at peak performance.
The team also oversees data center operations, including server management, storage, and networking equipment, to ensure the reliable delivery of health services.
Additionally, it manages databases with a focus on data security, availability, and top-tier performance.

title: Network / Hybrid Connectivity Engineer
description_clean:
We are seeking Network / Hybrid Connectivity Engineers to design, implement, operate, and troubleshoot network services that connect cloud, on-premises, shared-service, mission, and security-domain environments.
This role will ensure that services and applications can communicate reliably across diverse deployment environments while maintaining appropriate network segmentation, access controls, security boundaries, and connectivity protections.
Engineers will work across networking, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, cybersecurity, and platform teams to design and maintain reliable connectivity for enterprise and mission services.
The ideal candidate brings strong enterprise networking expertise and the ability to troubleshoot complex connectivity issues spanning cloud, on-premises infrastructure, applications, and security boundaries.
Responsibilities
Hybrid Network Engineering
Design, implement, and support routing, DNS, load balancing, ingress, egress, and network segmentation across cloud and on-premises environments.
Engineer and maintain connectivity between AWS classified cloud environments and on-premises infrastructure.
Support connectivity between shared services, tenant environments, mission systems, and external dependencies.
Design and troubleshoot network paths across diverse deployment locations and infrastructure environments.
Coordinate AWS Direct Connect or comparable enterprise connectivity solutions where applicable.
Evaluate network dependencies and connectivity requirements for new and evolving platform capabilities.
Security & Boundary Integration
Partner with cybersecurity teams to implement approved network segmentation and Zero Trust patterns.
Coordinate firewall, proxy, boundary, and controlled-interface requirements across technical teams.
Support connectivity to cross-domain services while maintaining clear ownership boundaries with Cross-Domain Solution (CDS) specialists.
Document network dependencies, approved traffic flows, ports, protocols, and connectivity requirements.
Ensure network designs appropriately account for security controls and boundary requirements.
Operations & Troubleshooting
Troubleshoot complex network and application-connectivity issues across hybrid environments.
Support Kubernetes networking, service mesh, load balancers, and platform ingress/egress where applicable.
Participate in Tier 3/4 support, incident troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and scheduled maintenance.
Monitor network capacity, latency, availability, and recurring connectivity issues and recommend corrective actions.
Collaborate with application, platform, cloud, security, and infrastructure teams to resolve issues that span multiple technical domains.
Support network lifecycle activities as environments, tenants, and platform capabilities evolve.
Location: This position is fully onsite in Chantilly, VA

Active TS/SCI clearance with CI Polygraph.
Approximately 6-10 years of experience in enterprise, data-center, cloud, or hybrid networking.
6+ years' of experience with a BS, an additional 4 years may be considered in lieu of a degree.
Strong knowledge of TCP/IP, routing, DNS, firewalls, proxies, and load balancing.

Terraform, especially bringing existing resources under infrastructure-as-code.

Data warehouses (e.g., Snowflake), ETL/ELT pipelines, or workflow orchestration tools (e.g., Prefect, Airflow).

Fintech, lending, payments, banking, or another highly regulated environment.

True Zero Technologies, a veteran-owned small business, was founded on the principle that the purposeful enablement of people and technology in an organization directly ties to the quality of its outcomes.
True Zero recognizes that those outcomes begin and end with our people, and that is what we have built a community of like-minded, driven, and passionate individuals and innovators who are aligned in a common goal of delivering top-tier services to our customers.

The Cyber Security Analyst will be responsible for monitoring and responding to active threats and alerts occurring on customer networks and being part of a next generation Security Operations Center (SOC).
Security Analysts will leverage various industry leading tools and methodologies to rapidly investigate potential threats, building new professional skills and capabilities along the way, all the while providing superior service to our customers.

Deploy and secure security systems, application layer and traditional firewalls, vulnerability management and forensics utilities, and other infrastructure deployed and maintained by the Information Security Office.
Develop plans to safeguard information against unauthorized access modification, and destruction, and ensure organizational continuity of operations.
Work with SIEM solutions such as Splunk and others to perform investigation and triage of incidents.
Working with your team and broader True Zero community to stay up to date on the latest security trends and threats to improve the effectiveness of security programs for our customers.
Following processes and procedures and providing refinement suggestions for them.

title: DevOps Engineer
description_clean:
On a mission to deliver affordable, delightful healthcare for all, First Stop Health provides connected, whole-person virtual care to employers 24/7 through app, website, or phone in all 50 states.
First Stop Health prioritizes an engaging and easy-to-use experience, setting people on healthier journeys through care at multiple stages.
We are proud to be recognized as one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies.
For those that choose to waive medical coverage a monthly medical waiver allowance will be provided.
The First Stop Health membership benefit is another added perk for employees and provides our virtual care solutions -- Urgent Care, Mental Health, and Primary Care -- from their very first day!
Job Description
First Stop Health runs a growing AWS platform.
It is a set of containerized microservices on ECS, event streaming on Kafka, and a long-running Django/Celery application that we are steadily moving onto modern delivery practices.
Everything we run in dev, staging and production is defined as code and shipped through automated pipelines.
You will be the newest member of a small, hands-on cloud team.
You will own well-scoped pieces of the platform from the start, and take on larger ones as you prove out.
You will write Terraform, maintain GitHub Actions pipelines, keep services healthy and help make releases boring.
This role suits an engineer who has already shipped infrastructure in a real environment and is ready to take more ownership of production, in a team that reviews changes carefully and values writing things down.
Responsibilities
Write and review Terraform for AWS resources (ECS Fargate, IAM, S3, KMS, Secrets Manager, ALB, Cloud Map, MSK, RDS) using reusable modules and per-environment stacks.
Build and maintain CI/CD in GitHub Actions: reusable workflows, OIDC-based AWS authentication (no long-lived keys), environment-scoped deploy roles, and build-once, promote-by-digest releases across dev, staging and production.
Help move legacy delivery tooling (AWS CodePipeline/CodeBuild) onto GitHub Actions, including task-definition templating and automated rollback on failed deploys.
Carry production changes through our gate: produce a plan, get it reviewed, then apply.
Keep dev, staging and production consistent, and detect and resolve drift.
Operate containerized services: monitor service health, read logs to diagnose failures, investigate failed deployments and unhealthy targets, and document what you learn.
Support observability: Datadog agents and log shipping, CloudWatch alarms and service health checks.
Help close the gaps in service-health alerting.
Contribute to our multi-account AWS foundation, managed with Atmos and Terraform components (networking, DNS, SSO and team roles, ECR, ECS, Aurora, ElastiCache, backups and logging), including pull requests, automated plans and applies, and drift detection.
Help keep us audit-ready: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, backups, encryption and access reviews, working with our compliance tooling (Vanta).
Work with the application teams on event-streaming infrastructure (Kafka on MSK, topics, IAM grants, consumer groups and Debezium change data capture).
Apply least-privilege IAM and sound secrets handling.
Never expose secret values or sensitive data in code, logs or pull requests.
Take part in a rotating on-call (PagerDuty) schedule for production.
You will respond to alerts, triage with the runbooks, escalate when needed, and write up what happened afterwards.
New team members shadow the rotation before taking a primary shift.
Keep runbooks and architecture notes current, and write clear pull requests that explain the what and the why.
Requirements
2 to 4 years of experience in cloud, DevOps, platform or site reliability work, or equivalent hands-on experience.
Working knowledge of AWS, including ECS or another container platform, IAM, S3, VPC networking and CloudWatch.
Hands-on Terraform (or a comparable infrastructure-as-code tool): modules, remote state, and reading a plan critically before applying.
Experience building CI/CD pipelines, preferably GitHub Actions.
Comfort with Docker and containerized workloads.
Solid Git skills (branching, rebasing, resolving conflicts, pull-request review) and the command line (bash).
Scripting in Bash or Python, and fluency with JSON and YAML, including tools such as jq.
Willingness to join a rotating on-call schedule, and a calm, methodical approach to incidents.
Clear written communication, and the habit of checking your work against logs and real state rather than assumptions.
Nice to Have
Experience with Atmos, Terragrunt or another tool for managing Terraform across many accounts and stacks, and with Cloud Posse components or Geodesic.
Experience with ecspresso, AWS CDK or CloudFormation, or other ECS deployment tooling.
Familiarity with AWS Organizations and multi-account patterns: IAM Identity Center (SSO), SAML or Entra ID federation, Transit Gateway, VPC design and DNS delegation.
Experience with AWS security and compliance services (CloudTrail, GuardDuty, AWS Backup, WAF) and with compliance platforms such as Vanta, in support of SOC 2 or HIPAA-style controls.
Exposure to Aurora/RDS Postgres, ElastiCache (Redis), SQS, DMS or Lambda.
Experience with self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, pre-commit hooks, terraform-docs and architecture decision records (ADRs).
Exposure to Kafka or managed streaming (MSK), or change data capture with Debezium.
Familiarity with Datadog or a similar observability platform.
Experience running Django or Celery applications in production, or working with PostgreSQL / Aurora.
Understanding of cross-account access patterns (for example, cross-account ECR pulls) and OIDC federation.
Experience in a regulated environment such as healthcare, and an understanding of why data-handling discipline matters.
An AWS certification (Solutions Architect Associate, DevOps Engineer Professional or similar).
Tools you'll work with
Cloud: AWS (ECS Fargate, ECR, MSK, Aurora/RDS, ElastiCache, S3, KMS, Secrets Manager, IAM Identity Center, CloudWatch)
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atmos, Geodesic, pre-commit, terraform-docs
Delivery: GitHub Actions (including OIDC and reusable workflows), ecspresso, Docker
Streaming and data: Kafka (MSK), Debezium, PostgreSQL
Observability, security and compliance: Datadog, PagerDuty, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Vanta
Applications you will support: Medplum-based services, a Django/Celery monolith, and Kong
How We Work
Production changes are gated.
Plan, human review, then apply.
Nothing reaches production as a side effect of other work.
Evidence over assumption.
We diagnose from logs and real service state, and we report outcomes honestly, including failures.
Security by default.
Least-privilege IAM, encrypted storage, private-by-default buckets, and no secret values in output.
Build once, promote everywhere.
The artifact tested in dev is the artifact that reaches staging and production.
Write it down.
Runbooks, pull-request descriptions and lessons learned are part of the job.
Review is normal.
Infrastructure changes are reviewed by a peer before they ship.
Shared on-call.
The team rotates production on-call through PagerDuty, so no one carries it alone.
Why join us
Real ownership of production infrastructure, with a team that reviews and teaches.
Meaningful work: reliable systems that support members' access to care.
A modernization effort in progress, so you will see the full arc from legacy to automated delivery.
First Stop Health is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Research shows that women, people of color and other historically underrepresented groups tend to only apply to jobs in which they meet all the job requirements.
Unsure if you check every box?
Apply.
We would love to consider your unique experiences and how you could make First Stop Health even better.
To learn more about First Stop Health, visit www.fshealth.com and if you require any assistance during the application process or have questions, please don't hesitate to contact our talent acquisition team via email at careers@fshealth.com

Identify, document, and track defects through resolution.
